notes: Summary: SyntaCraft builds an IDE-first copilots platform used by internal developer teams and 3rd-party customers. Extremely latency-sensitive: dev UX expects token streaming <30ms perceived latency for inline completions.
Primary ask: Dedicated capacity for peak developer hours (US/EU) + burst policy that scales on commit windows (10:00-12:00 / 16:00-18:00).
Model preferences: want ability to pin exact model versions per customer profile; rolling upgrades must preserve pinned model for current sessions.
Quote from CTO (02/12 call): "If completions lag when multiple devs hit autocomplete during releases, adoption drops overnight. We need predictable tail-latency and a clear fallback policy."
Security: VPC control plane required, KMS integrations mandatory, audit logs retained 13 months for enterprise customers. SSO via SAML (Okta).
Cost sensitivity: willing to pay for reserved throughput but need clear burst pricing and override caps. Interested in Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching/kv-caching tuned to IDE patterns.
Integration notes: Plugin uses streaming websocket for partial tokens; needs server-sent events fallback. Also uses embeddings for code search across monorepos (large repo vectors).
POC scope proposed: 1) 4-week performance benchmark vs current infra (self-hosted), 2) security questionnaire + pen-test summary, 3) cost projection for 6-month pilot (1000 dev-hours/day).
Decision criteria: latency (95p and 99p), availability during peak hours, predictable monthly committed spend, security sign-off.
Internal stakeholders: CTO (A. Navarro), Head of Platform (M. Singh), Lead SWE (K. Alvarez) — all attended demo 01/20.

technical_requirements: SLOs: 95p token latency <40ms, 99p <120ms under committed throughput
Dedicated pool with burst multiplier up to 2.5x for 2–3 hour windows
Per-customer model pinning API + migration plan for pinned sessions
Streaming protocol: websocket + SSE fallback; partial token flush required every 15ms for editor UX
KV/prefix caching across sessions to speed completions for recurrent code patterns
Quantization recommendations acceptable if no regression >2% top-n token accuracy for completions
